body.summary: A nested, self-referential novel about imprisonment, translation and the refusal to repeat a wound. Anne Twenty-Six lives in a tower inside a crash built by the alien shade Michael, who wants her to teach him the 'trick' that lets humans break his worlds. Elsewhere, Grant and Azad are thawed from the Mooncrash into a suburban house run by the shade Sylvie, while Cordelia, once a student in the Chester Chrestomath crash, becomes a Wolf Squadron agent under Hector Stein. Twenty-Seven (formerly Twenty-Six) learns she is the author of the Nowhere-to-Hide event that poisoned the world, and is ordered by Hector to rebase reality itself. ||She refuses, choosing a self-selecting rebase that leaves history scarred but intact, and the book ends with the collaborators finishing their manuscript.||

arcs.summary: Twenty-Six is taken from her tower by Cordelia, becomes Twenty-Seven, and is pressed by Michael to discover the trick that breaks crashes.
Grant and Azad are thawed from the Mooncrash into Sylvie's house, where Grant becomes addicted to a game and Azad is later freed.
Cordelia trains as a Wolf, falls for Twenty-Seven, and hides her link to the Ells and Sylvie.
Hector Stein wages war on the beasts and the Silence, and orders Twenty-Seven to rebase reality.
Twenty-Seven refuses Hector twice, learns the truth of the Nowhere-to-Hide event, and performs a self-selecting rebase.

notable_scenes.summary: Cordelia opens the box in a bathroom stall and becomes a shrivel in a vast, recoiling space.
The blue woman with the sword takes Anne from Michael's tower.
Grant meets the goopball and learns that everything is different from everything else.
Twenty-Seven delivers her monologue to Michael explaining that bilaterals harden under strain.
Sylvie, scarred and grinning, writes his essay on the Mirzakhani field in silence.
Twenty-Seven arbitrates with Arthur the raccoon and learns of the undo-button trick.
Twenty-Seven speaks to Twenty-Six in a dream and plays Move 77.
